profile.headline: Research Software Engineer at Stanford University
profile.summary:
Website: https://alexander-baker.com

- Mechanical engineer with 10+ years experience in biomedical research and 8+ years in biomechanical computational research.

- Experienced communicator and writer with 5 first author publications, 7 conference presentations, and teaching assistant to 4 undergraduate engineering courses including orthopaedic biomechanics.

- Designed and executed large computational studies with subject-specific finite element modeling to validate workflows against clinical and benchtop results.

- Interested in using  models to answer challenging questions.

positions.title: Mechanical Engineering Tutor
positions.description: Short term role designing biomechanical engineering focused research prompts and evaluation criteria using Gmsh and FEBio implicit FEA simulations.

positions.title: Postdoctoral Researcher
positions.description: Developed tooling and pipelines to extract risk metrics and evaluate fracture risk in elderly populations using clinical data

positions.title: Doctoral Student
positions.description:
- Secured a grant to design and perform bench-top testing of 16 femurs to develop a new computational/experimental statistically efficient approach for paired testing (Galliker et al. VPH 2026)

- Performed several analytical studies to investigate the predictive ability of novel finite element model-derived biomarkers (Baker et al. J Biomech in review; Baker et al. ESB 2024; Baker et al. ESB 2023). These studies involved statistical analyses including regression modeling, ROC analysis, and variance-based sensitivity analysis. The biomarkers are in use with current collaborators and have been used to secure follow-up funding.

- Developed and distributed a Python package to automate the construction and analysis of finite element models from clinical CT data. Reduced model builds from weeks to hours, enabling large-scale cohort level analyses.

- Co-authored studies, delivering statistical analyses and model results (Praveen et al. Osteoporos Int 2025; Bjornsson et al. CMBBE 2023; Fleps et al. Bone 2022).

positions.title: Research Engineer
positions.description:
- Served as the group’s primary researcher for a U.S. Army-funded project to develop a biofidelic anthropomorphic test device for underbody blast (WIAMAN). Often led working group meetings with collaborators and presented findings to stakeholders.

-  Developed a novel statistical estimator which used ROC analysis to compensate for biased experimental observations (Baker et al. J Biomech 2018).

- Used LS-Dyna, ANSA, R scripting, and Python scripting to develop finite element models for the WIAMAN project (Baker et al. J Biomech Eng 2021).

- Supported development and benchtop validation of a new finite element model of the Schutt Air Pro XP football helmet (Decker et al. Ann Biomed Eng 2020).

positions.title: Biomedical Research Engineer
positions.description:
Worked on a 1 year project to correlate bending strength of the distal femur with area moments of inertia calculated from dual x-ray absorptiometry (DXA) scans. 

Designed and built an experimental setup for an MTS 858 Minibionix and performed 3-point bend tests on cadaver femurs.

Wrote Matlab scripts to generate pixel based bone mineral density maps from DXA scan data.

Project resulted in a journal publication in Annals of Biomedical Engineering and a poster at the American Society of Biomechanics Annual Conference 2016 in Raleigh, NC

projects.title: Finite Element Analysis of an Individual Trabecula in Bending: A Parameter Study (M.S. Project)
Senior Design Project (Autonomous Bulk Transport Vehicle)

publications.title: A Method to Measure Predictive Ability of an Injury Risk Curve using an Observation-Adjusted Area under the Receiver Operating Characteristic Curve
Pixel-Based DXA-Derived Structural Properties Strongly Correlate with pQCT Measures at the One-Third Distal Femur Site
